record.context_brief: Finite omitted values obstructing Herman rings
record.original_question: If a general transcendental meromorphic function has a finite omitted value, does that condition alone force the map to have no Herman rings of any period?

evidence.quote: We propose the following conjecture. Conjecture: If a general meromorphic function has a finite omitted value, it does not have a Herman ring of any period.

However, no known example exists of a function that omits a value and possesses a Herman ring. This has led to the conjecture that a meromorphic function with an omitted value cannot have a Herman ring.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}=\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a transcendental meromorphic function. The Fatou set $F(f)$ is the set of points $z\in\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ at which the iterates $\{f^n\}$ form a normal family in some neighbourhood of $z$ (where defined). A periodic Fatou component $U$ of period $p\ge 1$ (so $f^p(U)=U$ and $f^k(U)\ne U$ for $0<k<p$) is called a Herman ring if $U$ is conformally equivalent to a round annulus $\{1<|w|<r\}$ and $f^p|_U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of that annulus.

A point $a\in\mathbb{C}$ is called a finite omitted value of $f$ if $a\notin f(\mathbb{C})$, i.e., the equation $f(z)=a$ has no solution in $\mathbb{C}$.

Question: Is it true that every transcendental meromorphic function $f$ which possesses at least one finite omitted value has no Herman ring of any period $p\ge 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The full conjecture appears to remain open. Partial results are known: meromorphic functions with a finite omitted value cannot have Herman rings of period 1 or 2, and functions whose omitted value is a pole have no Herman rings at all. No example of a meromorphic function with both an omitted value and a Herman ring has been constructed, but a proof for all periods is not available in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Omitted values and dynamics of meromorphic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the relationship between omitted values and Fatou components of meromorphic functions, including non-existence of Herman rings under certain conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes partial non-existence results for Herman rings of meromorphic maps with omitted values.

status_evidence.title: Herman rings with small periods and omitted values
status_evidence.snippet: Proves that meromorphic functions with an omitted value cannot have Herman rings of small period.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the conjecture for periods 1 and 2, leaving general periods open.

status_evidence.title: Herman rings of meromorphic maps with an omitted value
status_evidence.snippet: No known example of a meromorphic function with an omitted value possessing a Herman ring.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated but not fully proved.
